title: Hypha textual-notation keyword reference
description: Each textual grammar's keywords and operators, the productions that write them and the metaclasses whose syntax includes them, read from the release's own BNF. Generated by tools/knowledge-gen into knowledge/<tag>/textual-notation/keywords.json.

tag.description: The release the grammars were read from.

grammars.description: Keyed "kerml" or "sysml", as in cross-references.json. A grammar the release does not ship is left out.

entries.description: Keyed by the literal as the grammar writes it, e.g. "ref" or ":>>". Plain punctuation (; , { } ( ) [ ]) and the literals of the lexical productions declared before RESERVED_KEYWORD are left out. The sysml table also holds the literals of the KerML productions it calls without defining, unless SysML writes them itself; the counts include them.

kind.description: "reserved" when RESERVED_KEYWORD declares the word, "contextual" for another word, "operator" for a symbol.

syntaxFrom.description: The grammar whose productions write the literal: the grammar holding the entry, or "kerml" in the sysml table for a literal only the KerML productions SysML calls without defining (its expressions) write, such as "and" or "+".

productions.description: The productions of syntaxFrom whose own text writes the literal. Empty for a reserved keyword no production uses.

metaclasses.description: The metaclasses whose syntax includes the literal: written by a production that builds the metaclass, or by one it reaches through bare calls (a reference that is not the value of an assignment, into a production building nothing or the same metaclass or a supertype). Empty when the literal is only ever an assigned value, such as an enumeration literal or an expression operator.

via.description: "direct" when a production building the metaclass writes the literal itself, "helper" when only a production it calls does.

productions.description: The productions building the metaclass that reach the literal.

through.description: The productions reached from them that write the literal.
